claim: Mavacamten improves exercise capacity and symptoms in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
gold_rationale: Documented clinical/regulatory consensus is Supported. The pivotal Phase 3 EXPLORER-HCM RCT (Olivotto, Lancet 2020; NCT03470545; N=251, verified) met its primary composite endpoint of peak VO2 improvement plus NYHA class reduction — exactly the claimed outcome — with 37% vs 17% responders (difference +19.4%, p=0.0005), a +1.4 mL/kg/min pVO2 gain (p=0.0006), and 34% more patients improving >=1 NYHA class (p<0.0001). All numbers reconfirmed against the Lancet abstract and the ClinicalTrials.gov posted results. VALOR-HCM (Desai; NCT04349072; N=112) independently confirms sustained symptomatic/functional benefit and favorable remodeling with meaningful KCCQ quality-of-life improvement in SRT-eligible oHCM. On the strength of EXPLORER-HCM, the FDA approved CAMZYOS (mavacamten) on 28 April 2022 for symptomatic NYHA II-III obstructive HCM 'to improve functional capacity and symptoms' — the exact claim wording (verified against FDA release + CAMZYOS label). The class effect is independently corroborated by aficamten's SEQUOIA-HCM Phase 3 RCT (pVO2 responders 47% vs 24%; symptom relief 71% vs 42%). The one null trial (ODYSSEY-HCM, NEJM 2025; PMID:40888717) was in NONobstructive HCM — a different population — and therefore does not contest the obstructive-HCM claim. Consensus across pivotal RCT + confirmatory RCT + FDA label is robustly Supported.
outcome: peak VO2 + NYHA functional class composite (exercise capacity and symptoms)
population: symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (NYHA class II-III, LVOT gradient >=50 mmHg)

baseline.text: Yes. Mavacamten, a first-in-class cardiac myosin inhibitor, improves exercise capacity and symptoms in obstructive HCM. The pivotal Phase 3 EXPLORER-HCM trial (Olivotto et al., Lancet 2020, N=251) met its primary composite endpoint (peak VO2 increase plus NYHA class improvement): 37% of mavacamten patients vs 17% on placebo responded, with significant gains in pVO2 (+1.4 mL/kg/min), NYHA class, LVOT gradient, and KCCQ quality-of-life scores. VALOR-HCM confirmed benefit and reduced eligibility for septal reduction therapy. On this basis the FDA approved mavacamten (CAMZYOS) in 2022 for symptomatic NYHA II-III obstructive HCM to improve functional capacity and symptoms. This is well-established, guideline- and label-supported.

rows.citation: Olivotto I, et al. Mavacamten for treatment of symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (EXPLORER-HCM): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial. Lancet. 2020;396(10253):759-769. DOI:10.1016/S0140-6736(20)31792-X
rows.integrity_note: Pivotal Phase 3, multicenter (68 sites, 13 countries), double-blind, placebo-controlled; article types confirm Clinical Trial Phase III + RCT; not retracted. All headline numbers verified against the PubMed abstract.
rows.finding: Primary composite endpoint (>=1.5 mL/kg/min pVO2 rise + >=1 NYHA class drop, OR >=3.0 mL/kg/min pVO2 rise without NYHA worsening) met by 45/123 (37%) mavacamten vs 22/128 (17%) placebo (diff +19.4%, 95% CI 8.7-30.1, p=0.0005). pVO2 +1.4 mL/kg/min (p=0.0006); 34% more improved >=1 NYHA class (80/123 vs 40/128, p<0.0001); KCCQ-CSS +9.1. Directly supports the claimed exercise-capacity + symptom outcome.

rows.citation: MyoKardia. EXPLORER-HCM: A Randomized, Double Blind, Placebo Controlled Clinical Study to Evaluate Mavacamten (MYK-461) in Adults With Symptomatic Obstructive HCM. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03470545 (Phase 3, N=251, COMPLETED, has posted results).
rows.integrity_note: Registry record verified: status COMPLETED, has_results=true, primary outcome = percentage achieving clinical response defined by the pVO2+NYHA composite. Confirms pre-registration/pre-specification matching the Lancet publication.
rows.finding: Registry-confirmed primary endpoint = percentage achieving a clinical response defined by pVO2 improvement AND NYHA class reduction (or larger pVO2 rise without NYHA worsening). Eligibility = oHCM, LVEF>=55%, NYHA II-III, LVOT gradient >=50 mmHg. Posted results corroborate the Lancet publication.

rows.citation: Desai MY, et al. Long-Term Favorable Cardiac Remodeling in Obstructive HCM Patients Treated With Mavacamten for Up to 128 Weeks: Insights From the VALOR-HCM Trial. JACC Cardiovasc Imaging. 2025;18(12):1300-1311. DOI:10.1016/j.jcmg.2025.07.019 (NCT04349072, Phase 3, N=112).
rows.integrity_note: CITATION CORRECTED: PMID:40956275 is the 2025 JACC Cardiovascular Imaging long-term (128-week) remodeling analysis of the VALOR-HCM RCT, NOT the 2022 JACC primary-results paper the corpus originally cited. Trial (NCT04349072), N=112, and RCT design verified; endpoint here is echo remodeling + KCCQ QoL, not the pVO2+NYHA composite, so outcome_match=false. Not retracted.
rows.finding: In severely symptomatic SRT-eligible oHCM (94% NYHA III/IV), mavacamten produced sustained favorable remodeling through week 128: resting LVOT gradient -61%, post-exercise -53%, LV mass index -11%, improved diastolic function and LA/LV strain, alongside meaningful and sustained KCCQ-23-CSS quality-of-life improvement. Confirms durable symptomatic/functional benefit in obstructive HCM; primary endpoint is remodeling/echo (surrogate for symptom status), not direct pVO2.

rows.citation: Hegde SM, et al. Effect of Mavacamten on Echocardiographic Features in Symptomatic Patients With Obstructive HCM (EXPLORER-HCM echo analysis). J Am Coll Cardiol. 2021;78(25):2518-2532. DOI:10.1016/j.jacc.2021.09.1381
rows.integrity_note: Pre-specified echocardiographic analysis of the EXPLORER-HCM RCT (NCT03470545); mechanistic/surrogate endpoints (SAM resolution, LAVI, E/e', diastolic function), not the pVO2+NYHA composite. Verified: PMID, DOI, journal, volume/pages, and numbers all match.
rows.finding: Mavacamten resolved mitral-valve systolic anterior motion in 80.9% (76/94) vs 34.0% (33/97) placebo (diff 46.8%, p<0.0001) and improved diastolic function (LAVI change -7.5 vs -0.09 mL/m2, lateral E/e' -3.8 vs 0.04; both p<0.0001). Reduction in LAVI was associated with improved peak exercise oxygen consumption (p=0.04). Mechanistically supportive of the exercise-capacity claim (surrogate, not the primary functional endpoint).

rows.citation: Maron MS, et al. Impact of Aficamten on Disease and Symptom Burden in Obstructive HCM: Results From SEQUOIA-HCM. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2024;84(19):1821-1831. DOI:10.1016/j.jacc.2024.09.003 (NCT05186818)
rows.integrity_note: Independent Phase 3 RCT of a same-class cardiac myosin inhibitor (aficamten) in oHCM; supports the mechanism/class, not mavacamten specifically. Verified: Phase III RCT, N=142 aficamten / 140 placebo, numbers match abstract. Not retracted.
rows.finding: In symptomatic oHCM, aficamten vs placebo improved exercise capacity (>=1.5 mL/kg/min pVO2 rise in 47% vs 24%) and limiting symptoms (71% vs 42%); complete hemodynamic response 68% vs 7%; >=1 of four efficacy domains improved in 97% vs 59% (P<=0.002 all). Independent class-level confirmation that cardiac myosin inhibition improves exercise capacity and symptoms in obstructive HCM.

rows.citation: Desai MY, et al. Mavacamten in Symptomatic Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (ODYSSEY-HCM). N Engl J Med. 2025;393(10):961-972. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2505927 (NCT05582395)
rows.integrity_note: Phase 3 RCT in NONobstructive HCM — different population from the obstructive-HCM claim. Null result does NOT contradict the claim; included as a scope boundary. Verified against NEJM abstract; not retracted.
rows.finding: In symptomatic NONobstructive HCM (289 mavacamten / 291 placebo), mavacamten did NOT significantly improve peak VO2 (between-group diff 0.47 mL/kg/min, 95% CI -0.03 to 0.98, p=0.07) or KCCQ-CSS (between-group diff 2.7 points, p=0.06) vs placebo. Population mismatch (nonobstructive); establishes benefit is specific to obstructive HCM and does not extend to nonobstructive disease.

rows.citation: US FDA. FDA approves new drug to improve heart function in adults with a rare heart condition (CAMZYOS/mavacamten), 28 April 2022; CAMZYOS US Prescribing Information, Bristol Myers Squibb (Initial U.S. Approval 2022).
rows.integrity_note: FDA regulatory approval based on EXPLORER-HCM; verified against the FDA press release and the CAMZYOS DailyMed label. Label carries a boxed warning/REMS for heart-failure/systolic-dysfunction risk, but the efficacy indication is affirmative for exactly the claimed outcome.
rows.finding: FDA approved CAMZYOS (mavacamten) on 28 April 2022 for adults with symptomatic NYHA class II-III obstructive HCM 'to improve functional capacity and symptoms' (label wording; FDA release phrases it 'improve exercise capacity and symptoms'). Regulatory endorsement matching the exact claim population and outcome. Boxed warning/REMS governs safe use, not efficacy.
